definitions.gloss: to barricade oneself in; to hole up; to shut oneself in
definitions.explanation: To take refuge inside a building or enclosed space and refuse to come out, often in a standoff situation. Commonly used in news reports about hostage situations or sieges. Can also be used more casually for shutting oneself in a room.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}がビルに{立|た}てこもった。
examples.english: The suspect barricaded himself in a building.

examples.japanese: {人質|ひとじち}を{取|と}って{銀行|ぎんこう}に{立|た}てこもる{事件|じけん}が{起|お}きた。
examples.english: An incident occurred in which someone took hostages and barricaded themselves in a bank.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}{前|まえ}は{部屋|へや}に{立|た}てこもって{朝|あさ}から{晩|ばん}まで{勉強|べんきょう}していた。
examples.english: Before exams, I'd shut myself in my room and study from morning till night.

notes:
Godan verb (ら row): {立|た}てこもる・{立|た}てこもります
て-form: {立|た}てこもって
た-form: {立|た}てこもった

Also written as {立|た}て{籠|こ}もる with the kanji {籠|こ}もる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビルに{立|た}てこもる (to barricade oneself in a building)
- {人質|ひとじち}を{取|と}って{立|た}てこもる (to take hostages and barricade oneself)
- {部屋|へや}に{立|た}てこもる (to shut oneself in a room)
- {立|た}てこもり{事件|じけん} (a barricade/siege incident)

USAGE:
Frequently appears in news reports about criminal incidents. In casual usage, it can describe someone who shuts themselves in a room to concentrate on something, though {引|ひ}きこもる is more common for that.
